content: NHS Wales is the official corporate entity of the National Health Service in Wales. It was originally part of the unified National Health Service shared with England but has since become a devolved system. NHS Wales, known in Welsh as GIG Cymru, is managed and operated by the Health and Social Care Department of the Welsh Assembly Government. Most residents of Wales have access to a District General Hospital, which offers a variety of medical services, including outpatient care, inpatient care, and day case procedures. Some of these hospitals are equipped to provide highly specialized services, such as burn treatment, plastic surgery, and cardiac surgery. Additionally, NHS Wales delivers community-based healthcare services, which include district nursing, health visiting, midwifery, and therapy services such as speech therapy, physiotherapy, and occupational therapy. In 2003, Local Health Boards (LHBs) were established to replace the previous Health Authorities in Wales. A typical Welsh NHS Trust oversees the administration of all hospitals within a specific region, as well as the provision of community care and mental health services. There are 12 regional NHS Trusts in Wales, each responsible for groups of local authority areas. In addition, there is a dedicated Trust for the Welsh Ambulance Service and another, Velindre NHS Trust, which manages national-level agencies and services. The University Hospital of Wales, located in Cardiff, serves as the primary teaching hospital for the country. Another key component of NHS Wales is Health Commission Wales, an executive agency of the Welsh Assembly Government. This organization is responsible for the centralized planning and funding of tertiary care and other highly specialized medical services. It also provides expert advice and guidance on specialist services to other parts of NHS Wales. Furthermore, NHS Direct is available in Wales, offering a telephone-based service where callers can choose to communicate in either Welsh or English.
